reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown treat the Esau hatred in Malachi 1:3 as relative non-election, not positive malice, keeping it consistent with God's essential love.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll presses the tension between a God who commands love of enemies yet is said himself to hate whole nations.

quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (1881), on Malachi 1:3.

quotes.text: Is it possible that God will hate his enemies when he tells us that we must love ours?
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (1881), on 1 John 4:8.

sides.verseText: but Esau I hated, and made his mountains a desolation, and gave his heritage to the jackals of the wilderness.\"
He who doesn't love doesn't know God, for God is love.
